study_identification.title: Brain morphology normative modelling platform for abnormality and centile estimation: Brain MoNoCle

study_characteristics.study_objective: To present a user-friendly, open-source web platform for normative modeling of brain morphology, pre-trained on a large healthy control dataset, and to validate its utility in clinical cohorts.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ADHD1000; BLISS; CamCAN; Chronotype; Greene-HM; HCP; MEGUK; NCL-dementia; NIMH-IHV; NKI; OASIS3; Stanford-CR; UCLH)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Outliers were detected statistically using GAMLSS models (residuals > 5 median absolute deviations) and visually by plotting hemisphere-level brain metrics against age for each dataset. Listwise deletion was performed on flagged outliers.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: GAMLSS models were used to simultaneously model the parameters (mean, standard deviation, skew, and kurtosis) of the distribution as response variables of the explanatory variables sex, age, and scanning site/batch. The mean and standard deviation depended on sex (fixed effect), site (random effect), and a smooth function of age. The skew depended on sex (fixed effect) and a smooth function of age, and the kurtosis depended on a smooth function of age.

response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness; Cortical volume; Pial surface area; K; I; S

predictor_effects.answer: Fixed effects for sex; random effects for site; smooth function for age.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study uses GAMLSS to model mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis as functions of covariates, including site as a random effect, which explicitly handles nuisance structure.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Generalized additive models for location scale and shape (GAMLSS) using the gamlss package (https://cran . r - project . org / web / packages / gamlss/) were used to simultaneously model the parameters (mean, standard deviation, skew, and kurtosis) of the distribution as response variables of the explanatory variables sex, age, and scanning site/batch. Specifically, in our model, the mean depends on sex (fixed effect), site (random effect), and a smooth function of age; the standard deviation depends on sex (fixed effect), site (random effect), and a smooth function of age; the skew depends on sex (fixed effect) and a smooth function of age; and the kurtosis depends on a smooth function of age.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study performed a subsampling analysis to assess model stability.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We performed a subsampling analysis that showed our models stabilised, see Supplementary Materials S3 for details.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not mention validation on an independent dataset from the same domain.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study validated the model on two clinical datasets (bipolar disorder and temporal lobe epilepsy) which are different domains from the healthy control training data.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: To demonstrate the utility of our normative models in predicting abnormalities in patient groups and individuals, we included two exemplar clinical datasets. A sample of 133 adults with mesial TLE (mTLE; n = 74 right hemisphere seizure onset; n = 59 left hemisphere seizure onset) and 99 healthy controls (HC- mTLE) were acquired from the recent IDEAS dataset release ( P . N. T aylor et al., 2024), which was approved by a Research Ethics Committee (22/SC/0016). We also included a sample of 56 adults with bipolar disorder (BD) and 26 healthy controls (HC- BD) from the Bipolar Lithium Imaging and Spectroscopy Study (BLISS) ( Little et al., 2024; Smith et al., 2018).

diseases_studied.answer: Bipolar disorder (BD); Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (mTLE)

clinical_groups_sex.answer: BD: F 35 (62%); mTLE left: F 43 (58%); mTLE right: F 39 (66%)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group-level differences were assessed using Cohen's d. Individual-level abnormalities were validated by comparing z-score differences between hemispheres with clinical seizure lateralization.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The Brain MoNoCle platform provides a user-friendly interface for normative modeling of brain morphology, and its outputs align with existing literature and clinical data, highlighting the importance of investigating multiple morphology metrics.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study presents Brain MoNoCle, a web-based normative modeling tool for brain morphology. The tool was validated using a bipolar disorder cohort, where it produced results more consistent with large-scale studies than traditional case-control comparisons. In a temporal lobe epilepsy cohort, the tool replicated group-level findings and showed that individual-level abnormalities in cortical volume and isometric size (I) could predict seizure lateralization with over 75% accuracy. The study also found that the novel morphometric 'K' showed the best model fit for age and sex (R2=0.8) compared to other metrics.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The normative dataset, while large, could benefit from more sites with diverse global representation. The current version uses a single brain parcellation and does not support longitudinal data.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The platform allows for the analysis of multiple morphology measures, including novel independent components (K, I, S), which can provide insights not captured by traditional metrics like cortical thickness.
